24.t: Working with data: switching off the light
q: Describe the changes in RuBP and GP in the first 60 s of darkness. Use figures.
RuBP falls from 10 to 2; GP rises from 10 to 19 (almost doubles).
Explain why GP rises in the dark.
Rubisco still fixes CO₂ to RuBP, making GP, because this step needs no light. But GP cannot be reduced to triose phosphate without ATP and reduced NADP from the light-dependent reactions.
Explain why RuBP falls in the dark.
RuBP is still being used up, but it is regenerated from triose phosphate, which needs ATP. With no ATP, no new RuBP is made.
Predict and explain the changes if, instead, the CO₂ supply were cut off in the light.
RuBP rises and GP falls: RuBP is still regenerated but no longer used, while GP is still reduced but no longer made.
Explain why both levels return to their starting values after 150 s.
The light reactions supply ATP and reduced NADP again, so GP is reduced and RuBP regenerated at the original rates.
